paragraph_checks.label: Macro Stance
paragraph_checks.reviewed_text: The uncomfortable US combination is weaker manufacturing and higher long yields. Reuters reports the manufacturing slump extending while inflation pressures ease; the ISM release puts its manufacturing PMI at 48.5 index points. [[n2386]] [[n2381]] Disinflation improves the eventual policy argument, but an activity slowdown can reach earnings before financing becomes cheaper. Companies serving industrial customers therefore need an identifiable margin or market-share bridge. A valuation case based entirely on the Federal Reserve rescuing demand is less compelling when the bond market is demanding more compensation at the long end. Treat lower input pressure as a potential benefit that must be checked against order weakness. Reuters also reports cooling May inflation improving hopes for a Fed cut. [[n1729]] The favourable price signal and weaker manufacturing are consistent with a cooling economy, but their portfolio implications diverge if the growth slowdown becomes more severe than the expected financing relief. Require companies to explain both sides of that equation.
